newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan money rates end sharply down, seen stable.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan money rates end sharply down, seen stable.

text.p: Taiwan's money rates finished sharply lower on Friday despite the central bank's issue of T$3.0 billion in one-month negotiable certificates of deposit to soak up liquidity, dealers said.
Dealers said money that flowed out in early March was returning to fuel the banking system.

The overnight interbank rate closed at 6.363 percent against Thursday's 6.814 close, still well outside the central bank's 5.0-5.5 percent target zone, with 30-day commercial paper down to 6.25 percent from 6.75.
The overnight interbank rate had risen for 10 consecutive sessions before Friday's decline.

Dealers said they did not expect further sharp falls as the central bank was expected to continue to issue NCDs to tighten liquidity with the aim of slightly cooling down Taiwan's red-hot stock market.
The interbank rate was expected to move between 6.000-6.500 next week, they added.
The stock index closed higher again on Friday, gaining 7.42 points to end at a six-year high of 8,275.57, although its rate of rise has flattened out in recent sessions.
The bond market reported no trade in the afternoon session, bond traders said the central bank's attitude would determine the market's direction next week.
The central bank has repeatedly said it would not change its stable-to-loose monetary policy, but many analysts suspected the bank may move to tighten the money policy soon.
